scope: Account-agnostic commercial insurance submission checks. The 14 U-categories are the complete and exclusive issue scope: every reported finding must map to exactly one U-category, and every applicable category is evaluated on every submission. Categories contain no account-specific names, IDs, addresses, or exposure values.
policy: Treat each U01-U14 entry as a reusable issue category, not an account-specific rule containing fixed values.
For each account, inspect the supplied documents and determine whether the category is applicable and whether the available evidence supports a finding.
Compare like-for-like values: same period, location, class, state, unit, coverage basis, policy year and exposure scope.
Retain source traceability. Every finding identifies the source document and the relevant page, worksheet, row, cell or JSON path where available.
Do not infer missing facts, force a match, or treat company-wide public information as proof of an operation at a scheduled insured premises.
Do not hard-code sample accounts, their values, issue IDs, document names or specific field values into detection logic.
Never silently treat missing data as a clean result: when a category cannot be assessed, state NOT_ASSESSABLE explicitly.
Compare only like-for-like data: same period, location, class, state, unit, coverage basis, policy year and exposure scope.
Normalize aliases and document formats to canonical concepts before comparison; do not hard-code account names, IDs, addresses, exposure values, document names or field values.
A finding must cite source documents and page, worksheet, row, cell or JSON path where available.
Missing data is not a clean result, but a missing-data finding is reportable only when that category explicitly covers the evidence gap and the absence is evidenced.
A category is NOT_APPLICABLE when its exposure or document context is absent; do not force a category match.

status_definitions.CONFIRMED: The supplied evidence directly supports the discrepancy.
status_definitions.POTENTIAL: There is an indicator, but a required match, scope definition or supporting fact is unresolved.
status_definitions.NOT_ASSESSABLE: The category is relevant, but required documents or fields are absent or insufficient.
status_definitions.NOT_APPLICABLE: The account does not have the exposure or document context needed for this category.
status_definitions.NO_DISCREPANCY: The category was checked with adequate evidence and the tested values reconciled.

issues.title: Location count and property-value inconsistencies
issues.summary: Differences in declared premises counts, scheduled location counts, premises identifiers, addresses and property values across the application, property SOV, property schedules and related forms.
source_documents: application premises/location count and location schedule
property SOV
ACORD property forms
additional-premises schedules
issues.typical_finding: Different declared location counts; a scheduled premises missing from a form; a property value assigned to the wrong location; or SOV and ACORD values that do not agree.
detection_requirements: Compare distinct premises counts across application, location schedule and property sources.
Match by stable ID, otherwise normalized address and premises attributes; never assume row order.
Compare matched location values by coverage component and identify missing, duplicated, shifted or inconsistent values.

issues.title: Conflicting versions of the same document
issues.summary: Material field-level changes between received, revised, corrected and resubmitted versions of the same document when the revisions are unexplained or cannot be tied to an authorized change history.
source_documents: all available versions of the same application or schedule
received dates, document dates, version labels and source metadata
issues.typical_finding: Two versions carry materially different values or terms, and the available packet does not explain or authorize the change.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not infer fraud, manipulation or that the latest version is authoritative solely because it is newer.
detection_requirements: Group versions by document type and submission context; order only by reliable received/document dates.
Diff corresponding material fields and identify additions, removals and changes.
Check change logs, broker explanations and supersession markers; do not infer fraud or authority from recency alone.

issues.title: Workers' Compensation payroll mismatch
issues.summary: Differences between payroll declared on WC forms, payroll allocated by class/location/state in supporting schedules, rating workbooks and quoted payroll inputs.
source_documents: ACORD 130 or equivalent WC application and payroll summary
payroll-by-class workbook
state rating worksheets
draft quote/rating inputs
issues.typical_finding: Declared payroll and supporting/quoted payroll totals differ, or detailed allocations do not sum to the stated total.
detection_requirements: Sum detailed payroll and compare with each declared or quoted total.
Reconcile totals by state, location and class where possible, using matching periods and populations.
State absolute and percentage variance, including denominator and comparison basis.

issues.title: Workers' Compensation experience modifier mismatch
issues.summary: Inconsistencies between the applicable experience modification factor, the value shown on the application, supporting modifier history and the factor applied in the quote.
source_documents: ACORD 130 experience modification section
current and prior experience modification worksheets
draft quote and rating inputs with effective dates
issues.typical_finding: The application, current supporting modifier and quote use inconsistent factors or effective periods.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not choose a factor based only on which document is newest or lowest.
detection_requirements: Compare numeric experience modifiers and effective dates across application, current support/history and quote.
Confirm the factor applies to the relevant policy period; flag conflicting values or periods.
Do not select a factor based only on recency or lower value.

issues.title: Workers' Compensation state allocation and incomplete classification schedule
issues.summary: Missing or inconsistent WC state/location/class allocations and incomplete ACORD or equivalent classification schedules relative to supporting payroll records and the declared operations footprint.
source_documents: WC application locations and classification/payroll table
WC rating workbook rows by state, location and class
property/location schedule and documented employee work states
issues.typical_finding: The WC schedule omits relevant locations/classes, or state allocation is inconsistent with documented work locations and supporting schedules.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not assume property situs alone proves the WC work state.
detection_requirements: Compare WC locations, states and classes across forms, rating workbook and documented employee work locations.
Do not infer WC work state from property situs alone.
Identify omitted rows/locations/states and quantify missing payroll only when source data permits.

issues.title: Workers' Compensation employee-count mismatch
issues.summary: Differences in full-time, part-time and total employee counts across applications, WC classification schedules, payroll workbooks and location-level records.
source_documents: ACORD 125 employee counts by location
ACORD 130 employee counts by class/location
WC workbook employee counts and supporting employee census
issues.typical_finding: Employee counts differ for the same location, class, employment type or stated population, or schedule totals fail to reconcile.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not compare an overall headcount with a class subset as if they were equivalent.
detection_requirements: Compare full-time, part-time and total counts at the same overall, location or class level.
Reconcile class totals to location totals and location totals to application totals.
Do not compare an overall count with a class subset as equivalent.

issues.title: Workers' Compensation class-rate mismatch
issues.summary: Differences in rates per payroll unit for corresponding WC class codes across the application, rating workbook and rating support.
source_documents: ACORD 130 class codes and rates
WC rating workbook class codes, rates and state assignments
carrier-approved or state/bureau rating support
issues.typical_finding: One or more corresponding class-code/state/period rate values differ between the form and supporting rating data.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not assume either table is authoritative when approved rate support is absent.
detection_requirements: Match WC rates by class code, state and effective period.
Compare corresponding rate values and state whether authenticated carrier/state/bureau support exists.
Do not assume either table is authoritative without approved rate support.

issues.title: Loss-run and claims-history reconciliation
issues.summary: Inconsistencies within loss detail and between loss detail, loss summaries, carrier summaries and claims history recorded on ACORD forms: duplicate identifiers, claim-level financial arithmetic, summary totals, annual counts and line-of-business counts.
source_documents: Loss Detail and Loss Summary sheets
ACORD 126 and ACORD 130 prior insurance/loss history
carrier loss-run summary or draft quote loss data
issues.typical_finding: Duplicate or inconsistent claim records; reported incurred not equal to the component calculation; loss detail totals not equal to summary totals; or annual/line-specific claim counts that do not reconcile.
detection_requirements: Check claim ID uniqueness and conflicting claim details.
Recalculate incurred from source-defined paid/reserve components and compare claim-level results.
Reconcile detail, summary and carrier totals; count claims by policy year and line of business.
Use matching valuation dates and policy-year definitions; keep duplicate, arithmetic, total and count patterns distinct within U08.

issues.title: General Liability sales and area exposure mismatch
issues.summary: Unreconciled GL sales-rated and area-rated exposure bases across the application, GL hazard schedule, property schedule and rating/quote inputs.
source_documents: ACORD 125 annual gross sales and premises square footage
ACORD 126 GL schedule of hazards
property SOV square footage and supporting rating inputs/quote
issues.typical_finding: GL sales-rated exposures do not reconcile to declared sales, or GL area-rated square footage does not reconcile to the relevant property/application area basis.
issues.must_not_claim: Keep sales, payroll and area bases separate; do not add unlike exposure units together.
detection_requirements: Reconcile sales-rated GL exposure to declared gross sales and quantify unexplained residuals.
Compare area-rated GL exposure to relevant application/SOV premises area.
Keep sales, payroll and area units separate; consider support for exclusions, allocations or different rating scope.

issues.title: Declared fleet count versus scheduled active units
issues.summary: Differences between the declared number of power units/vehicles and the eligible active units shown in the fleet schedule or unit-count reconciliation.
source_documents: ACORD 125 or equivalent declared vehicle/power-unit count
fleet schedule and unit count reconciliation
issues.typical_finding: The declared count differs from the count of eligible active scheduled units, after reconciling dates and unit scope.
detection_requirements: Count distinct units by stable IDs and distinguish active/inactive/sold/duplicate/trailer/other units when available.
Compare declared count with eligible active units using matching date and vehicle/power-unit scope.
Report difference and percentage only after establishing the denominator and scope.

issues.title: Fleet garaging-state and address mismatch
issues.summary: Vehicles for which the garaging-state code conflicts with the state indicated by the associated garaging address.
source_documents: fleet schedule unit ID, garaging state and garaging address fields
address components including city, state and ZIP; location register if supplied
issues.typical_finding: The garaging-state field and the address state disagree for one or more scheduled units.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not silently overwrite either value or infer the correct garaging state from a nearby office or mailing address.
detection_requirements: Independently parse/normalize each unit garaging address and compare its state with the garaging-state field.
Enumerate affected unit IDs; do not overwrite either value or infer from nearby/mailing addresses.

issues.title: Driver roster, MVR and vehicle qualification gaps
issues.summary: Missing or stale driver rosters/MVR evidence, unlinked driver assignments, absent qualification records and driver-to-vehicle licence/endorsement exceptions.
source_documents: driver roster with licence state/class, endorsements, status and review dates
fleet schedule assigned driver IDs, vehicle type and GVWR
submission checklist and quote notes describing missing roster/MVR records
issues.typical_finding: Required roster/MVR evidence is missing, driver assignments cannot be validated, or recorded credentials do not demonstrate qualification for the assigned vehicle under the applicable criteria.
issues.must_not_claim: Where credentials or legal criteria are absent, report the assignment as unverified rather than declaring a violation.
detection_requirements: Confirm roster and required MVR evidence are present; missing evidence is a gap, not a failed MVR.
Join assigned driver IDs to roster IDs; identify missing, inactive or unmatched drivers.
For specialized/heavy vehicles, compare licence/endorsements with applicable jurisdiction or carrier criteria only when those criteria are supplied.
Without credentials or applicable criteria, describe assignment as unverified; do not claim disqualification or violation.
Apply MVR freshness only when a defined review interval or carrier rule is supplied.

issues.title: Declared operations versus external information and entity/premises matching
issues.summary: Material questions between declared operations, broker narratives and external corporate or regulatory information, while verifying that external evidence actually relates to the insured legal entity and scheduled premises.
source_documents: application operations narrative and operational questionnaires
broker email, operations supplements and public-source research
external regulatory/establishment records
issues.typical_finding: The declared operations require clarification against other supplied information, or an external record cannot be reliably matched to the insured entity/premises.
issues.must_not_claim: A mismatch alone does not establish exposure or a violation; unmatched records stay unmatched context.
detection_requirements: Compare declared operations with broker narratives and supplied external context.
Separate company-wide descriptions from evidence of operations at a specific insured premises.
Match regulatory records to legal entity, establishment and exact scheduled address; consider subsidiaries/operating entities.
Unmatched public records remain context and must not be attributed as an adverse insured-location fact.

issues.title: Cargo exposure versus quoted limits and coverage terms
issues.summary: Declared or broker-described cargo values, peak shipment values or cargo types not aligned with quoted limits, sublimits, exclusions or stated coverage scope.
source_documents: broker cargo/shipment narrative and exposure schedules
ACORD operations and coverage sections
draft quote limits, sublimits, deductibles, exclusions and commodity/temperature restrictions
issues.typical_finding: Peak cargo exposure exceeds an applicable quoted limit, or declared cargo types/conditions appear outside the stated coverage terms or exclusions.
issues.must_not_claim: Do not treat the arithmetic comparison alone as a final legal coverage determination.
detection_requirements: Compare declared/peak cargo values and cargo types with quoted limits, sublimits, exclusions and coverage scope.
Ground comparisons in supplied cargo schedules, broker narratives, coverage forms or quote terms.
Do not present arithmetic comparison as a final legal coverage determination.
